topic: 11/11 in Korea: Pepero Day (Busan schoolgirls c.1993-94, Pepero launched 1983, Lotte marketing from 2000s, 2025 Pepero sales forecast ₩241.5B incl. ~₩100B overseas), Garaetteok Day (Ministry of Agriculture since 2006), Farmers' Day (土 = 十一, 1996), convenience-store gift sets and homemade Pepero, anti-graft law bans student gifts to current teachers (ACRC Q&A 2026-05-12)
title: In Korea, 11/11 Is a Snack Holiday

slides.headline: In Korea, **11/11** is a snack holiday.
slides.note: But not everyone agrees on the snack.

slides.headline: First, **Pepero Day**
slides.body: Friends and couples trade thin chocolate-dipped sticks called Pepero (빼빼로). Four 1s in a row look like four sticks.

slides.headline: Started by **schoolgirls**
slides.body: Around 1993, middle school girls in Busan began swapping the sticks with a wish: grow tall and slim like a Pepero. The snack itself came out in 1983.

slides.headline: The rice cake **answer**
slides.body: Farm groups pushed back with garaetteok (가래떡), a long white rice cake that also looks like a 1. Since 2006, the agriculture ministry has called 11/11 Garaetteok Day.

slides.headline: Officially, it's **Farmers' Day**
slides.body: Split the Chinese character for soil into its strokes, and you get the characters for ten and one. Korea made 11/11 Farmers' Day in 1996.

slides.headline: Stores go **all in**
slides.body: Convenience stores stack giant gift sets out front, often tied to dolls and balloons. Many students skip the store and dip their own sticks in melted chocolate.

slides.headline: Not for **your teacher**
slides.body: Under Korea's anti-graft law, students may not give gifts to the teachers who grade them, even small ones. A handwritten note is fine.

slides.headline: Pepero sales Lotte expected **in 2025**
slides.body: About $170 million, around ₩100 billion of it from abroad.

slides.headline: Sweet, or **just marketing?**
slides.body: Some schools ban Pepero swaps, and critics call it a candy company's holiday. Fans say it's the cheapest way to tell someone you care.

slides.headline: Korea, explained **by a Korean.**
slides.body: Follow for the context behind the things Korea does.
slides.graphic: Long white rice cakes and chocolate sticks side by side on a wooden table, blurred behind the text.

caption:
In Korea, November 11 is Pepero Day, when people trade chocolate sticks.

But the same date is also Garaetteok Day and Farmers' Day, and there's one person a student can't give Pepero to.

Who would you give yours to?
reply: One more thing: 11/11 is also the day Korea's navy was founded, in 1945. What does 11/11 mean where you live?
fact_check: 2-3장: 빼빼로 1983년 출시(문화일보), 1993~94년 부산·영남 여중생 '빼빼로처럼 키 크고 날씬하게' 교환 유래(YTN 2021-11-11, 아이뉴스24).
5장: 농업인의 날 土=十一, 1996년 제정(뉴시스 2016-11-11, 시대일보). 1997 기재 기사도 있음.
6장: 편의점 대형 선물세트·인형 결합 진열, 홈메이드 빼빼로(일반 관행).
7장: 청탁금지법, 담임·교과교사에게 학생 선물은 5만원 이하도 불가, 손편지는 가능(권익위 Q&A, 파이낸셜뉴스 2026-05-13, korea.kr 148926371).
8장: 2025 빼빼로 매출 전망 2415억(해외 약 1000억) 머니투데이 2025-11-08·뉴스토마토. 환율 약 1,420원 가정.
